stem: A crop response appears shortly after a feed change, but root-zone pH also shifted and the plants entered a new developmental stage. What is the strongest diagnostic approach?
choices: Evaluate nutrient interactions, developmental context, root-zone chemistry, and the timing of all changes before assigning the response to one element or concentration.
Attribute the response to the feed change because it happened most recently.
Ignore developmental stage because nutrition operates independently of plant stage.
Use only the fertilizer label rate because root-zone measurements cannot affect nutrient interpretation.
rationale: Nutrient responses can reflect interactions among supply, stage, root-zone conditions, and environment; temporal association alone does not prove a single cause.
